cards.text: We're near the end of a love song, friend, a song full of two lovers praising each other (Song of Solomon 4:1-7; 5:10-16). Now a voice asks who this is, coming up and leaning on her beloved. The only thing I ever leaned on was a pile of takeout menus in a junk drawer.

cards.question: She's coming up, leaning on her beloved. Where is she coming up from?

cards.text: Then the song says, "I roused you under the apple tree; there your mother conceived you; there she travailed and brought you forth."
Then a big request: "Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm…" As a cookie stamper, I RESPECT anybody who wants to leave a mark.

cards.question: The request is to be set as a seal over the heart. What reason does the song give right after it?

answers.text: Love is as strong as death

cards.text: Its jealousy is as unrelenting as Sheol, and its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all. I work next to ovens ALL DAY, friend, and even I'm taking a step back.

cards.question: Love's sparks are the fiercest blaze of all. True or false: the song is saying love burns out fast.
Love burns that hot. So what can mighty waters do to it?

answers.text: They put it out in time

cards.text: Rivers can't sweep it away either, and then the song talks money: a man giving all the wealth of his house for love. Somebody once bought ME for a quarter at a closing sale, so I am VERY invested in how this goes.

cards.question: A man offers all the wealth of his house for love. True or false: the song says his offer would be utterly scorned.

cards.text: Then the song shifts: "We have a little sister…" and she's still young. I raised six little cookie cutters, friend, so I have BEEN in a family huddle about the little one.

cards.question: The speakers have a little sister who is still young. What are they wondering about her?

answers.text: What to do for her when she is spoken for
How to keep her at home for good
Who should teach her the old songs

cards.text: Here's the plan: if she is a wall, they'll build a tower of silver on her, and if she is a door, they'll enclose her with panels of cedar. Silver towers and cedar panels, friend, and the fanciest thing anybody ever put around ME was a dish towel.
Then a woman speaks up: "I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers."

cards.question: The woman says she is a wall. What does she say she has become in the eyes of the man she speaks of?

answers.text: Like one who is far away

cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel (1 Kings 4:1), had a vineyard in Baal-hamon, and each tenant had to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit. A THOUSAND shekels, friend, and I break a sweat when the flour bill shows up.

cards.question: Solomon's tenants each owe a thousand shekels for his vineyard's fruit. Then the speaker says, "But my own vineyard is mine to give…" True or false: the speaker says the thousand shekels are for Solomon.
The thousand shekels go to Solomon. Who gets the other two hundred?

cards.text: Then a call goes out: "You who dwell in the gardens, my companions are listening for your voice…"

cards.question: The companions are listening for the voice of the one in the gardens. True or false: the speaker asks that voice to stay quiet.

cards.text: And here it is, friend, the very last line of the whole Song of Solomon, and it invites the beloved to come away. The last invitation I got came from an angel at the back of a junk drawer, and I said yes so fast I almost left my mustache behind.

cards.question: The last line invites the beloved to come away. The beloved is asked to be like what on the mountains of spices?

answers.text: A gazelle or a young stag
